html:
SMTO-EXE-0057 — The program SMTO was about to use has closed or restarted

GUID: ad61201c-4f9d-5e82-927e-b0bf8f02653f
Slug: desktop-stale-process
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • The program SMTO was asked to work with has closed or restarted since SMTO last looked, so SMTO stopped rather than risk acting on the wrong program.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Gateway computer, check whether the program is still running. If you wanted it closed and it's gone, you're done. The program may have closed on its own before SMTO acted.
  2. Ask SMTO to list the running apps again (for example "which apps are open?") and confirm the one you mean. A program that restarted gets a new identity, so SMTO must look it up again before acting.
  3. Then ask SMTO for the action on the program it just found. SMTO acts only on a program it has just confirmed, so it can't hit a different one by mistake.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the program in a fresh list and the requested action completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't ask SMTO to act on a program by its number alone; numbers can be reused by different programs.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Desktop process identity no longer matches a live process: the PID exited, its creation time differs (PID reuse or restart), the signed identity is invalid (e.g. after a Gateway restart), or the macOS application process is absent.

What this means

  • The process disappeared, its encoded PID/creation-time identity no longer matched, or the corresponding application process was absent. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • The process disappeared, its encoded PID/creation-time identity no longer matched, or the corresponding application process was absent.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect PID together with creation identity; never authorize a signal using the reused number alone.

How to fix it

  • Re-run desktop.process_info, desktop.processes or desktop.applications on the same Gateway to get the current pid and process_identity, review that it is the intended process, and authorize any new action with that fresh identity. Never act on a PID alone; identities are invalidated by process restart, PID reuse and Gateway restart.
  • Inspect the PID again and review its new identity before authorizing a new action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the PID again and review its new identity before authorizing a new action.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended live process is identified and any new action uses its fresh identity.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
